summary: The DualRayRank method (dual-ray-based constraint ranking) does not outperform IIS-TopK under controlled comparison. On the truncation regime (IIS > K=5), both methods achieve 0/16 repair rate. Overall, both achieve 1/31 (3.23%) repair with the same instance. Best-of-2 inference scaling (65.12%) dominates all repair methods (max 58.86%) by ~6pp. The primary hypothesis is refuted and the approach needs reconsideration.
analysis: Under controlled conditions (same model Qwen2.5-7B, K=5, greedy decoding), DualRay-TopK (B) produces identical results to IIS-TopK (A): 1/31 repair rate, 0/16 on truncation regime, 58.17% end-to-end Pass@1. Adding Farkas weights (C) also yields identical 1/31. Under heavily optimized conditions (72B model, K=10, N=16, 2 rounds), repair rate improves to 7/31 (22.58%), but only 1/16 truncation regime instances is repaired. These improvements are confounded with model capacity (7B->72B), increased K (5->10), higher N (1->16), and iterative rounds. The truncation regime contains only 16 instances (<50 gate), making practical relevance weak. Best-of-2 with same 7B model achieves 65.12% vs 58.86% best repair, using far less compute.
reason: Three lines of evidence support the 'bad' verdict: (1) Zero improvement of DualRay-TopK over IIS-TopK under controlled conditions -- both achieve 0/16 on truncation regime and 1/31 overall, repairing the identical instance (EasyLP_425); (2) The truncation regime has only 16 instances, failing the 50-instance practical relevance gate; (3) Best-of-2 inference scaling strongly dominates all repair methods including the most optimized variants, indicating solver feedback repair is not competitive with simple re-sampling on this benchmark. The optimization phase showed that model capacity (72B) is the dominant factor, not the feedback signal type.
